# ICP reconciliation (Ateles): implementation-derived vs design-sourced views

## Subject

Whether the design-sourced view of who Ateles is for agrees or disagrees with the implementation-derived ICP, and specifically whether excluding 'teams or multi-operator organizations' from the anti-profile is a design boundary or a build-state description.

## Summary

Reconciles two independently-derived views of who Ateles is for, following Neotoma's own icp_reconciliation.md method: the implementation-derived ICP (docs/icp.md, projected as target_persona ent_fd64f687e7e1bf5711c6de2b) audits what the code currently does; the design-sourced ICP (target_persona ent_b6e066a5d110b8500d3ec8c9) audits what docs/foundation/ states the system is designed to be. The two AGREE on the P1 solo-operator profile in full detail. They DISAGREE on one point: whether 'teams or multi-operator organizations' belong in the anti-profile. Verdict: that anti-profile line is a description of the CURRENT BUILD (P1 only is implemented), not a DESIGN boundary — the design's own roadmap names multi-operator as Phase 2 of one continuous system, ruled in detail (authority_model.md decisions 48-50; multi_tenant.md decisions 79-83), not a hypothetical extension. Excluding the design's own intended future from the anti-profile is a positioning error, not a fact the implementation-derived ICP is entitled to assert as durable.

## Method

Applied Neotoma's icp_reconciliation.md method directly (read via git -C ~/repos/neotoma show origin/main:docs/icp/icp_reconciliation.md, read-only): hold two independently-derived views, treat their agreement as a signal rather than collapsing them into one, and state disagreements explicitly rather than smoothing them over. Central warning carried over verbatim from Neotoma's O3 finding and applied here as a discipline check (see 'Applying Neotoma's O3 warning to Ateles' below): 'a functional audit reads investment and infers an intended buyer — but investment can also be infrastructure the product needs in order to keep its own promises, with no buyer behind it at all.' The design-sourced view (ent_b6e066a5d110b8500d3ec8c9) was derived from docs/foundation/charter.md, authority_model.md, multi_tenant.md, status.md, and decision_state.md/conformance.md at origin/main — read directly, not imported from docs/icp.md or any prior positioning doc, per the task's explicit instruction not to guess or import the answer.

## Body

## Agreement table

| Aspect | Implementation-derived view (docs/icp.md, ent_fd64f687e7e1bf5711c6de2b) | Design-sourced view (docs/foundation/, ent_b6e066a5d110b8500d3ec8c9) |
|---|---|---|
| P1 archetype | Solo technical founder-operator running a company/life through a governed agent swarm | Same — explicitly named 'the single-principal case of the multi-operator model' (README.md), i.e. P1 of the design |
| Core JTBD | Operate, Govern, Remember, Extend, Trust the dangerous parts | Identical five objectives, sourced from the same charter.md, restated for a system built to eventually hold more than one accountable human |
| Stack/substrate | claude CLI/Claude Code + MCP, Python, Neotoma, launchd/Docker, SOPS+age, self-provisioned keys | Same substrate — and the design states explicitly it was 'deliberately built so the single-operator case is not a dead end' and that multi-operator is 'an extension of the entity model... not a rewrite' |
| Ideal entry point | Stand up Neotoma + identities + capability grants + one daemon | Identical entry point; the design treats P1 as the necessary first phase of the same system, not a different starting point |
| Stage / build status | 'P2-P5 multi-operator phases designed but unbuilt' | Confirms and sharpens this: P2 is 'designed... nothing built' except decision C9 (operator entity) and multi_tenant.md §7's five decisions (79-83), all now ruled but with no runtime reader |

The two views were derived from disjoint inputs (a functionality audit of the running code vs. a reading of the design corpus) and they agree in full on the P1 profile. This agreement is the useful signal per Neotoma's method: the audience the design intends for phase 1 is the same audience the code currently, actually serves.

## Disagreement: the anti-profile's exclusion of teams/multi-operator organizations

docs/icp.md's anti-profile states: 'Teams and multi-operator organizations. The trust model assumes one operator behind every agent; multi-tenant separation is out of scope and would require multi-tenant Neotoma.' The implementation-derived target_persona (ent_fd64f687e7e1bf5711c6de2b, messaging_bad field) carries this forward verbatim, sourced explicitly and only from docs/icp.md.

**This is accurate as a description of the current build and inaccurate as a description of design intent, and docs/icp.md does not itself claim to speak to design intent.** Its own header states it is 'reverse-engineered from a first-principles audit of what the code in this repository actually does... not derived from the README, marketing copy, or any prior positioning doc' — i.e. it is scoped, by its own declaration, to exclude exactly the foundation documents that settle this question. Three independent pieces of design evidence contradict reading the exclusion as durable:

1. **README.md**: 'Today it assumes one operator who owns the machine, the keypairs, and the Neotoma instance — the single-principal case of the multi-operator model described below.' Single-operator is stated as a CASE of the general model, not the model's terminus.
2. **docs/foundation/status.md's roadmap table**: P2 'multi-operator identity and ownership' is explicitly named, cites authority_model.md, and its status is 'designed... nothing built' — the canonical designed-but-unbuilt signature used throughout the foundation, not 'undesigned' or 'out of scope by design.'
3. **docs/foundation/authority_model.md, decision 82** (ruled 2026-09-08, registered in conformance.md): 'Every instance may have one operator or many, whoever hosts it and wherever it is deployed, so multi-operator is a property every instance has and not a consequence of a hosting arrangement,' with multi_tenant.md §3's per-operator scoping dimension ruled 'load-bearing' rather than 'belt-and-suspenders.' Decisions 48-50 build the quorum/separation-of-duties mechanism specifically around counting DISTINCT HUMAN PRINCIPALS: 'two agents bound to one operator are one interest on a quorum,' and 'a solo operator's swarm can never satisfy a quorum of two... that is true of such a swarm, not a defect in the rule.' A mechanism built to require multiple distinct human principals, with the single-operator case named as the degenerate case that fails it by construction, is not a mechanism for a system that excludes multi-operator by design.

**Verdict: the anti-profile item is a BUILD-STATE fact, not a DESIGN boundary.** It correctly excludes teams/multi-operator organizations from what a fork can adopt and use TODAY (P2-P5 have no runtime reader). It incorrectly reads, if taken as durable positioning, as a claim that Ateles is not FOR teams/multi-operator organizations by design — the design's own roadmap says the opposite: P1 is explicitly the first phase of a system whose stated purpose (charter.md) is to let work be initiated, executed, and approved 'by humans and agents together' (plural humans), with structural mechanisms (quorum, separation of duties, per-human delegation) that are meaningless for a single operator and were built for more than one.

## Applying Neotoma's O3 warning to Ateles

Neotoma's O3 finding demoted a heavily-invested, SHIPPED surface (attestation/capability grants) to infrastructure because no buyer wanted it — the warning being that 'investment can also be infrastructure the product needs in order to keep its own promises, with no buyer behind it at all.' Checked against that warning here: does the multi-operator finding in this reconciliation commit the SAME error in reverse (inferring a buyer from investment that is actually just infrastructure)? No — the two cases are structurally different. O3's surface was BUILT with no named buyer in any market document. Here, the corpus does not merely invest engineering effort in multi-operator machinery incidentally; it explicitly NAMES the intended buyer in prose independent of any code investment — the charter's purpose statement ('humans and agents together,' plural), the README's 'single-principal case of... the model described below,' and status.md's own P1-P5 roadmap table, which exists specifically to communicate who future phases are for. This is a design STATEMENT, not an inference from unexplained code investment; the O3 trap does not apply because the evidence is textual and direct rather than inferred from what got built.

## Method note: what is DESIGN-canonical vs IMPLEMENTATION-canonical, per Neotoma's role assignment

Following Neotoma's canonical-roles section: for a public, functionally-grounded statement of who Ateles serves TODAY, docs/icp.md (and ent_fd64f687e7e1bf5711c6de2b) remains correct and should not be rewritten to claim capabilities that do not exist. For design intent and roadmap positioning — what an operator or prospective team should expect Ateles to become, and why today's single-operator build is not a dead end — the design-sourced view (ent_b6e066a5d110b8500d3ec8c9) and docs/foundation/ are canonical. Both should survive as separate, cross-linked artifacts exactly as Neotoma kept icp_from_functionality.md and the market docs separate rather than collapsing them.

## What remains genuinely unsettled

The foundation SETTLES that multi-operator is core design intent (P2 of one continuous system), not merely a nice-to-have. It does NOT settle, and this reconciliation does not invent an answer for: (1) P4's eight open questions on distributed authority and initiative, explicitly 'awaiting the operator' per status.md; (2) the default policy VALUES multi_tenant.md defers to Neotoma's own record-level design (within-tenant default visibility, capability ceiling of a non-owner operator — decisions 81 and 83 rule that these are Neotoma's to set, not Ateles's); (3) WHEN P2-P5 will be built, which is a roadmap/prioritization decision outside this reconciliation's scope. These are named here as open rather than resolved, per the task's instruction that a stopped run beats a fabricated answer — none of them bears on the anti-profile question this reconciliation was commissioned to answer, which the foundation does settle.

Reviewed by: architect.

## Gaps

This reconciliation did not independently re-derive or challenge the implementation-derived ICP's P1 content (core_jtbd, stack, entry point) — it was consumed as correct per the task's instruction to reuse rather than rebuild, and cross-checked only for consistency with the design-sourced view, which agreed on every P1 point. No customer-development or icp_signal evidence exists for either view on this Neotoma instance (consistent with the existing incumbent/pain-analysis entities' own stated gap), so this reconciliation is a design-vs-implementation textual analysis, not a market-validated one.
